blocks.orig: The Gombe Stream National Park is located on the western border of Tanzania and the Congo. Established in 1968, It is one of the smallest national parks in Tanzania with only 35 km2 of protected land along the hills of the eastern shore of Lake Tanganyika. It is a famous place for those who want to see chimpanzees off the beaten track. Guided hikes take visitors into the forest to see chimpanzees in the wild. The area has steep valleys and the forest vegetation ranges from grassland to forest and tropical rainforest.
blocks.html: Gombe Stream National Park sits on Tanzania’s western border with the Congo. Founded in 1968, it is among the smallest national parks in the country, protecting just 35 km2 of hills along the eastern shore of Lake Tanganyika. It is well known as a place to see chimpanzees away from the usual tourist routes: on guided hikes you head into the forest to watch chimpanzees in the wild. The terrain consists of steep valleys, and the vegetation shifts from grassland to forest and tropical rainforest.

blocks.orig: Jane Goodall’s research in the national park
blocks.html: Jane Goodall and her research in the park

blocks.orig: The Gombe Stream national park is the place where Jane Goodall did her research on chimpanzee populations. Jane Goodall first traveled to Tanzania in 1960 at the age of 26 with no formal college training. Her research proved the intellectual and emotional sophistication of the chimpanzees. Goodall set up a small research station in Gombe in hopes of learning more about the behavior of our closest relatives. There she spent months tracking the chimpanzee troops, particularly the Kasekela chimpanzee community. She observed their daily habits until she was slowly accepted by one troop and was allowed rare and intimate glimpses into chimpanzee society.
blocks.html: It was in Gombe Stream National Park that Jane Goodall carried out her research into chimpanzee populations. She first came to Tanzania in 1960, aged 26 and without any formal college training. Her work demonstrated how intellectually and emotionally sophisticated chimpanzees are. Hoping to learn more about the behaviour of our closest relatives, Goodall established a small research station in Gombe. She spent months there following the chimpanzee troops, in particular the Kasekela community, and observed their daily routines until one troop gradually accepted her and granted her rare, intimate insights into chimpanzee society.

blocks.orig: In 1967, the Gombe Stream Research Center (GSRC) was established to coordinate ongoing chimpanzee research in the park. Run mostly by a team of trained Tanzanians, the GSRC is the longest-running field study of an animals species in their natural surroundings.
blocks.html: The Gombe Stream Research Center (GSRC) was founded in 1967 to coordinate the continuing chimpanzee research in the park. Largely staffed by trained Tanzanians, the GSRC represents the longest-running field study of any animal species in its natural habitat.

blocks.orig: Gombe’s high levels of diversity make it an increasingly popular tourist destination. Besides chimpanzees, primates inhabiting Gombe Stream national park include beachcomber olive baboons, red colobus, red-tailed monkeys, blue monkeys, and vervet monkeys. Red-tailed monkeys and blue monkeys also hybridize in the area. The park is home to over 200 bird species and bushpigs too. And you can find many species of snakes and occasionally hippos and leopards.
blocks.html: Thanks to its great diversity, Gombe is becoming a more and more popular destination. Apart from chimpanzees, the primates living in Gombe Stream National Park include beachcomber olive baboons, red colobus, red-tailed monkeys, blue monkeys and vervet monkeys; the red-tailed and blue monkeys even hybridise here. The park also holds more than 200 bird species and bushpigs, as well as many kinds of snakes and, now and then, hippos and leopards.

blocks.orig: My name is Sammy and I am a guide at Gombe Stream National Park for 14 years. Most of our guests are amazed  when they first encounter a group of chimpanzees. Watching them from up close is a privilege that not many people have. The park is small but the amount of monkeys you can spot is impressive.
blocks.html: I am Sammy, and I have guided in Gombe Stream National Park for 14 years. Coming face to face with a group of chimpanzees for the first time leaves most of our guests amazed. Observing them from so close is a privilege few people get. The park may be small, but the number of monkeys you can see is remarkable.
